title: pricing-backcast-scratchpad
content:
Pricing back-of-envelope scratchpad — token math + tier ideas (personal notes)

Context / goals
- Quick backcast for hosted API pricing options to validate PLG funnel economics and guardrails for when to push Dedicated sale.
- Want a couple of simple tiers that map cleanly to unit economics, and rules-of-thumb for when to convert active usage to reserved capacity.
- Rough target: gross margin >= 60% on hosted, better for committed customers.

Assumptions (working)
- Models: r-instruct-3B (cheap), r-instruct-13B-8bit (mid), r-instruct-70B-q4 (expensive).
- Infra costs: include GPU amortized cost, storage, network egress, small infra overhead. These are placeholders to iterate.
- Customer-side: average request = 120 prompt tokens + 450 completion tokens = 570 tokens total (call this "typical chat event").
- Cache/prefix reuse: for many apps ~35% of tokens are cached/prefix and saved for repeated prompts (high variance).
- Batching & concurrency: reduces per-token cost by ~20% on average for PLG traffic versus single-request baseline.

Infra baseline numbers (placeholders)
- r-instruct-3B: GPU cost $1.50/hr, throughput 600k tokens/hr (batching) => cost per 1M tokens = (1.5 / 600k) * 1e6 = $2.50/1M
- r-instruct-13B-8bit: GPU cost $2.50/hr, throughput 360k tokens/hr => cost per 1M tokens = (2.5 / 360k) * 1e6 = $6.94/1M
- r-instruct-70B-q4: GPU cost $4.50/hr, throughput 150k tokens/hr => cost per 1M tokens = (4.5 / 150k) * 1e6 = $30.00/1M
- Infra overhead (storage, networking, KMS, control plane) add ~15% on top of pure GPU cost; include that later in blended numbers.

Effective per-event cost examples (no ingress egress)
- Typical event: 570 tokens. Using mid model (13B) with 35% cache and 20% batching benefit: effective tokens charged = 570 * (1 - 0.35) = 370.5 tokens. Then batching/ops reduces cost by 20% => effective billed-token-equivalent = 370.5 * 0.8 = 296.4 tokens.
- Cost per token for 13B = $6.94/1M => per-token = 6.94e-6. So cost per event = 296.4 * 6.94e-6 = $0.00206 (~0.206 cents)
- For 3B: per-token = 2.50/1M => 2.5e-6 => cost per event = 296.4 * 2.5e-6 = $0.00074 (~0.074 cents)
- For 70B: per-token = 30/1M => 30e-6 => cost per event = 296.4 * 30e-6 = $0.00889 (~0.889 cents)

Blended hosted unit economics (very rough)
- Example product mix (PLG early): 60% requests hitting 3B, 30% 13B, 10% 70B.
- Weighted cost per 1M tokens = 0.6*2.5 + 0.3*6.94 + 0.1*30 = 1.5 + 2.082 + 3.0 = $6.582/1M tokens. + infra overhead 15% => $7.57/1M tokens.
- If we aim for gross margin 65%, target price per 1M tokens = cost / (1 - 0.65) = 7.57 / 0.35 = $21.63/1M tokens.
- That seems high for PLG. Means we either need lower costs (better batching/caching), different mix, or subscription packaging to increase ARPU.

Pricing tier sketches (starter ideas)
- Free tier: 100k tokens/mo free, ideal for trial, includes limited rate.
- Starter (self-serve): $10/mo => 2M tokens included (equiv $5/1M). Overage $10/1M.
- Growth: $99/mo => 12M tokens included ($8.25/1M effective), overage $7/1M.
- Pro: $499/mo => 80M tokens included ($6.24/1M effective), overage $5/1M.
- Enterprise: custom pricing and committed volume with reserved capacity discounts (e.g., 40–60% off hosted list for >500M tokens/month and 12mo commit).

Quick checks vs unit costs from blend above (7.57/1M)
- Starter list-effective price $5/1M < cost -> subsidized acquisition. Acceptable if conversion path strong and average lifecycle value > CAC.
- Growth at $8.25/1M > cost -> modest margin. Pro $6.24/1M slightly below cost -> borderline. Need to tune included tokens or push commitment.
- Overage rates should be >= target price per 1M (e.g., $12/1M) to prevent heavy overage loss.

Ideas to reconcile economics (short list)
- Increase cache/reuse default across SDKs (aim to move average saved tokens from 35% -> 50%). Big win for multi-turn agents.
- Dynamic model routing: route low-cost traffic to 3B by default unless user requests higher fidelity or exceeds safety thresholds. Can cut blended cost significantly.
- Offer model-level pricing: users pick cheaper variants explicitly; default is cheaper model unless opt-in.
- Introduce a middle-layer subscription ("Generation Credits") that buckets tokens used for low-cost models at lower unit rates.
- Encourage local client-side context assembly (send only diffs) via SDK primitives to reduce prompt tokens in product integrations.

Rules-of-thumb / thresholds for Dedicated push
- If single org sustained > 150M effective tokens/mo on expensive models (13B/70B mix) -> propose Dedicated / Reserved conversation.
- If top-line hosted cost > 30% of ARR from that customer, evaluate dedicated pricing.
- For committed customers, offer tiered reserved discounts: 3mo: 15%, 6mo: 30%, 12mo: 45% off hosted list (numbers placeholder).

Open questions / TODOs
- Recompute throughput & cost numbers with actual infra billing (infra team to provide 1Q26 GPU amortization + network). (TODO: ask infra for runbook numbers, runbook ticket: JIRA-4671)
- Hook up model-specific cache ratios from runtime telemetry (what % of tokens saved per customer per month?). (TODO: Riley to add telemetry query)
- Evaluate competitor public list prices to ensure PLG starter price is defensible. Quick survey: OpenAI davinci pricing, Anthropic, Hugging Face inference endpoints — gather by 2026-03-10.
- Consider minimum overage price floor (e.g., $7/1M) to avoid heavy negative-margin overage.

Notes to self (fragments, quick heuristics)
- If average event cost < 0.2c then cheap enough for large-scale product features (token math suggests many 3B calls are <0.1c).
- Conversion funnel: free -> starter conversion at >50% of free cap usage. Consider gift credits to power first month of paid tier.
- Dedicated pricing should be an entirely different negotiation: price per GPU-hour + support + control-plane fee. Map their expected token consumption to required GPUs by throughput assumptions.

Slack references / context
- Pricing thread: #pricing-team — see the thread with initial asks from Solutions Eng (notes attached): slack:/pricing-team/threads/CL12345
- Conversation with CS: CUST-998 (big edtech pilot) wants 20B tokens over 6mo, mix looks heavier on 13B -> triggers Dedicated discussion.

Final quick summary (for next sync)
- Current rough blended cost ~ $7.5/1M tokens (very rough).
- Starter tier could be intentionally subsidized to drive PLG adoption, but we need a clear path to convert and a floor on overages.
- Key levers: routing to cheaper models, caching, batching, subscription packing, and reserved capacity for large accounts.

-- end scratchpad --

(Will clean up into a one-pager after infra numbers arrive.)
